summary: Initial and ongoing risk assessment (per NIST CSF) and documented cybersecurity best practices (e.g., CIS v8, COBIT 5, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST SP 800-53) within 90 days of licensure; documented incident response plan; incident reporting; 5-year record retention.
applies_to: Covered entities: nonrestricted licensees operating games, race books, sports pools and interactive gaming licensees in Nevada.
size_thresholds: Group I licensees (as defined in Reg 6.010(8)) must also designate a qualified individual, have an annual internal audit of cyber practices, and obtain an annual independent review and written attestation. Other covered entities are exempt from 5.260(5).
status: Amended Jan 29, 2026 (effective on adoption): 'cyber attack' replaced by 'cybersecurity incident', 24-hour Chair notice, 5-day initial report, 30-day updates.

summary: IT controls for Class II gaming systems: supervision, segregation of duties, logical and physical access, backups, change control.
applies_to: Tribal gaming operations conducting Class II gaming.
size_thresholds: Tiered by annual gross gaming revenue (25 CFR 543.2): Tier A >$3M-$8M, Tier B >$8M-$15M, Tier C >$15M; operations of $3M or less follow separate small-operation provisions (not itemized here).

summary: Written AML compliance program with internal controls, independent testing, training, and automated data processing systems for recordkeeping and SAR/CTR reporting.
applies_to: State-licensed and tribal casinos and card clubs.
size_thresholds: Only casinos/card clubs with gross annual gaming revenue over $1 million are 'financial institutions' under BSA (31 CFR 1010.100(t)(5)).

citation: PCI Security Standards Council standard (contractual, not law)
summary: 12 requirement families for protecting cardholder data; enforced through card-brand and acquirer contracts.
applies_to: Any merchant or service provider that stores, processes or transmits payment card data.
size_thresholds: Validation level (SAQ vs. QSA ROC) depends on annual card-transaction volume under card-brand merchant-level programs. Those levels are set by the card brands and were not verified here.
status: v4.0.1 published June 11, 2024 (PCI SSC blog). Not a law. Check for any later revision.

summary: FTC treats unreasonable data security and misleading privacy claims as unfair or deceptive practices.
applies_to: For-profit businesses. Under 15 U.S.C. 44, 'corporation' covers only entities organized for their own or their members' profit, so most nonprofits fall outside FTC Section 5 jurisdiction.

summary: Parental consent and (from Apr 22, 2026) a written information security program for children's data.
applies_to: Operators of child-directed online services and apps (games, streaming, theme park and family entertainment apps).
size_thresholds: Nonprofits exempt from FTC Act Section 5 are excluded from 'operator'.
status: Amended rule effective June 23, 2025; compliance Apr 22, 2026.
